nodes.description: Proxy implementation address persisted at storage slot keccak256("PROXIABLE") = 0xc5f16f0fcc639fa48a6947836d9850f504798523bf8c9a3a87d5876cf622bcf7; written by the constructor sstore and read by the fallback sload.
constructor(bytes constructData, address contractLogic): writes the logic address into the PROXIABLE slot and delegatecalls the supplied initialisation calldata, requiring success.
fallback() external payable: loads the stored implementation, forwards all calldata via delegatecall, and returns/reverts with the raw returndata.
delegatecall inside the constructor to an attacker-controllable contractLogic address with attacker-supplied constructData, executing arbitrary code in this contract's storage context.
delegatecall inside fallback() forwarding arbitrary calldata to the implementation address read from storage, allowing arbitrary delegatecalls and re-entrant calls back into the proxy.
assembly sstore writing the constructor-supplied contractLogic address into the PROXIABLE implementation slot without any validation or access restriction.
bytes memory constructData: raw initialisation calldata supplied to the constructor and forwarded verbatim to the delegatecall.
address contractLogic: caller-supplied implementation address used both as the sstore value and as the delegatecall target.
bool success: return flag of the constructor delegatecall, checked with require(success, "Construction failed").
let contractLogic := sload(PROXIABLE_SLOT): implementation address loaded from storage inside fallback() assembly.
let success := delegatecall(...): result flag of the fallback delegatecall, driving the switch between revert and return.

edges.reason: Attacker-controlled constructData parameter is passed directly as calldata to the constructor delegatecall, letting the caller execute arbitrary logic in the proxy context.
Attacker-controlled contractLogic parameter is used as the delegatecall target, allowing arbitrary code execution at construction time.
The unvalidated contractLogic parameter is written straight into the PROXIABLE implementation slot via assembly sstore, letting the caller set the proxy implementation.
The constructor executes the delegatecall to the supplied logic contract.
The constructor executes the assembly sstore that persists the implementation address.
The sstore operation writes the caller-influenced logic address into the PROXIABLE state slot.
The fallback sload reads the stored implementation address, which was set without validation from the implementation state variable.
The address loaded from storage is used as the delegatecall target, so control of the slot means control of all subsequent delegatecalls.
Every call reaching the fallback() body executes the delegatecall forwarding the raw calldata.
The success flag produced by the constructor delegatecall is stored in the local bool success.
The success flag produced by the fallback delegatecall is stored in the local variable success.
The constructor branches on the delegatecall success flag via require(success, "Construction failed").
The fallback switch on the delegatecall success flag decides between revert and return of the returndata.
The constructor delegatecall transfers execution to arbitrary logic that can re-enter this contract before initialisation is complete.
The fallback delegatecall hands full execution to the implementation, which can call back into the proxy fallback and re-enter state-changing logic.

normalization_plan.reason: The constructData parameter exists only to feed the constructor delegatecall calldata and has no independent meaning.
The contractLogic parameter is the delegatecall target in the constructor and defines the whole unsafe operation.
The success local is a transient return flag consumed by the constructor's require check.
The address read by sload in the fallback is only used as the delegatecall target, so it belongs to that unsafe operation.
The success local is a transient assembly flag consumed by the fallback switch statement.
